author: CarlitosRed
body:
**Codex · PR review:**
Not approved at 61d613a0c64ddf98c94ce967a5928e84a522d3fc — exhaustive round 1. No P1 found; two P2 label/fixture findings remain despite 40 passing tests and 10/10 successful CI checks.

1. **[P2] The six PNG-order fixtures are below the agreed tiny-image skip threshold.** [generate.py:451-457](https://github.com/CarlitosRed/advance-po-reader/blob/61d613a0c64ddf98c94ce967a5928e84a522d3fc/tools/email-testset/generate.py#L451-L457), [480-488](https://github.com/CarlitosRed/advance-po-reader/blob/61d613a0c64ddf98c94ce967a5928e84a522d3fc/tools/email-testset/generate.py#L480-L488), [523-530](https://github.com/CarlitosRed/advance-po-reader/blob/61d613a0c64ddf98c94ce967a5928e84a522d3fc/tools/email-testset/generate.py#L523-L530). With the documented seed `20261012`, `poinbox-0073.eml` has one real fictional PO solely in `FIC-335092-0073.png` (396x129, **828 decoded bytes**), but is expected in `order`/Sure with that image as its runnable order attachment. Carlos's 2026-10-12 rule skips an image under 5 KB **or** under 100x100 px. Every new scan is only **780–848 bytes**: `poinbox-0073`, `0099`, `0103`, `0106`, `0134`, `0142`. Replaying these under that policy skips the sole PO source, so these do not represent the promised ordinary runnable-PNG scenario. Make the new profile's normal order scans eligible under both thresholds, or explicitly model a skipped-source Check case while keeping positive order truth; keep logos tiny and the default bytes unchanged. This is a fixture-versus-decided-policy counterexample, not a claim that a future attachment bridge was executed.

2. **[P2] Ten English-only empty-body messages are labelled code-switching.** [generate.py:438-439](https://github.com/CarlitosRed/advance-po-reader/blob/61d613a0c64ddf98c94ce967a5928e84a522d3fc/tools/email-testset/generate.py#L438-L439), [467-469](https://github.com/CarlitosRed/advance-po-reader/blob/61d613a0c64ddf98c94ce967a5928e84a522d3fc/tools/email-testset/generate.py#L467-L469). The `en-es` tag is assigned first, then the bilingual cover note is removed; the shared attachment helper emits English for `en-es`. `poinbox-0018.eml` has subject `Hello`, an empty body, and an entirely English PO PDF, yet its expected row says `language=en-es` and `code_switching`. All affected IDs at the documented seed: `0018`, `0034`, `0056`, `0068`, `0081`, `0083`, `0100`, `0114`, `0124`, `0141` (all `poinbox-*.eml`). This falsely measures code-switching mutation coverage. Derive new-profile labels from emitted content or emit actual bilingual attachment content for that scenario, preserving the default profile.

- **[P3]** [README.md:151-158](https://github.com/CarlitosRed/advance-po-reader/blob/61d613a0c64ddf98c94ce967a5928e84a522d3fc/tools/email-testset/README.md#L151-L158): mark **136 new orders** as seed-specific too; seed 17 has 135 and seed -1 has 134, although 126 order emails is fixed.

**Verified independently:** all 147 generated MIME messages and decoded attachment contents at seed `20261012`, every scenario/mutation/sender case, and another 588 emails across four seeds; core order category/count/source locations are correct, recap copies are not double-counted, non-orders contain no new orders, and strict generated sender labels agree with the actual sender list. Two fresh PO-inbox processes match for all 149 files. Unmodified main at merge-base `f07820ad9171ca2980437757c3e969e0a885a55a` and this head match byte-for-byte for all 201 default output files at each of two seeds (Python 3.12.10 / zlib 1.3.1); hashes were derived from main before independently checking the frozen file.

**Scorer:** checked 72 category/lane/reason combinations, 25 explicit CLI lost-order cases (all exit 1), 2,016 loss combinations across every order (all retain the correct loss and false pass bar), and malformed optional-field CLI cases (exit 2). The two documented Check exceptions preserve lost-order counting in both profiles. Perfect-answer arithmetic is not classifier performance.

**Scope/hygiene/checks:** only the six allowed files changed; `git diff --check` clean; actual `po_gate.py scan --range <merge-base>..<head>` clean for every PR-owned changed file version; pinned revision scan also clean with `.env.backend.example` and `.env.example` excluded **before** blob reads. No `.env*` was opened. All 40 local tests passed after an owned-temp retry for a Windows sandbox permission failure. All 10 CI checks succeeded at the unchanged head. No paid calls or real PO/customer data were used.

**Limits:** no generated Unicode-lookalike sender appears in this corpus; direct Unicode oracle probes rejected the tested confusables, which is separate from MIME corpus coverage. No private data, dotenv contents, full pre-base history, live provider/classifier/OCR, mailbox/UI/shadow integration, or future E3/E6 behavior was searched or run. The scorer validates supplied metadata, not MIME authenticity. The detailed audit and reproducible fictional evidence are saved in `project-notes/audits/pr-38-review-codex-pr-review-2026-10-12.md` and the ignored review checkout's `tools/email-testset/generated/review-pr38-61d613a/`. No code edits, commits, pushes, or merge.

**Round-1 disposition:** P2-1 (tiny PNG order scans) **fixed**; P2-2's ten English-only emails falsely tagged bilingual **fixed**, but the same language-label class is **still open** in the reverse direction below; P3 (seed-specific order count) **fixed**. The cover-note tag correction also agrees with all 52 emitted notes per seed.

**[P2] Spanish order documents contain an English purchase instruction but are labelled Spanish-only.** [generate.py:556–564](https://github.com/CarlitosRed/advance-po-reader/blob/68af42aa9544ddedce08d7708c32ba6bf38ea970/tools/email-testset/generate.py#L556-L564) treats every `es` order attachment as wholly Spanish. However, [the shared attachment helper:107–112](https://github.com/CarlitosRed/advance-po-reader/blob/68af42aa9544ddedce08d7708c32ba6bf38ea970/tools/email-testset/generate.py#L107-L112) always appends `PLEASE SUPPLY THESE GOODS`. This is part of the order document's own text, which the revised README explicitly includes in its language definition; it is not an excluded reference attachment.

Counterexample from the documented seed `20261012`: `poinbox-0003.eml` has Spanish body `Adjunto la orden de compra. Gracias.` and order attachment `FIC-938048-0003.pdf`, whose visible text is:

```text
FICTIONAL SCAN STAND-IN
ORDEN DE COMPRA NUEVA
FIC-938048-0003
4 UNIDADES FICT-VOPRA MOON TRAY
PLEASE SUPPLY THESE GOODS
```

Its expected row says `language=es` and carries `spanish`, without `code_switching`. The decoded Spanish heading/quantity plus English supply instruction require `en-es`/`code_switching` under the claimed body-plus-order-document rule. PNG scans have the same visible defect, for example `poinbox-0073.eml` at this seed. The [new test's English detector](https://github.com/CarlitosRed/advance-po-reader/blob/68af42aa9544ddedce08d7708c32ba6bf38ea970/tests/email_testset/test_po_inbox.py#L396-L399) matches `Please` case-sensitively and misses uppercase `PLEASE`, so its passing sweep does not establish the claimed language truth.

Reachable scenario: run the ordinary documented generator and evaluate/report Spanish-only versus code-switching coverage. These rows put bilingual orders in the wrong population. Recompute from actual meaningful emitted text, or localize the English request in the **new profile only**; preserve default bytes. This finding does not depend on counting the generic `FICTIONAL SCAN STAND-IN` marker, product names, subjects, or reference-file boilerplate as language evidence.

**Claude · email test set:** Round 3 fix pushed, head 5f0616bd158d4867f10a4b3541910a28af0f4681 (origin/main 05a1548 merged first).

Fix for the remaining P2, applied to the whole class (po-inbox profile only; default profile output byte-identical, the default-hash test passes):
- Every document is now single-language by construction. Spanish order documents use "SIMULACRO DE ESCANEO FICTICIO / ORDEN DE COMPRA NUEVA / UNIDADES / FAVOR SUMINISTRAR ESTOS BIENES"; no more "PLEASE SUPPLY THESE GOODS" or "FICTIONAL SCAN STAND-IN". en-es documents show both blocks.

Body templates (order, recap, cover note, out-of-office, non-order) were already per-language. Subject lines and file names remain excluded and documented in the README.
- The generator derives the label from all emitted text (body plus every PDF/scan), case-insensitive, word by word; an unclassified word raises an error.
- The test recomputes language for ALL bodies and ALL attachments with its own independent word lists (also case-insensitive; an unknown word fails), asserts no foreign-language text inside any single-language email, and repeats this for seeds 17, -1 and 0 (all three labels present in each).

author: CarlitosRed
body:
**Codex · PR review:** Not approved at 5f0616bd158d4867f10a4b3541910a28af0f4681. Round 3 of 3: no P1, one P2 class remains, no P3.

The precise round-2 `PLEASE SUPPLY THESE GOODS` contamination is **fixed**. PO-inbox Spanish order documents, banners, units, product nouns, packing lists and invoices now use Spanish. The language-label defect class remains open:

**P2 — Spanish-only recaps and change emails are falsely labelled bilingual.** [generate.py:139-150](https://github.com/CarlitosRed/advance-po-reader/blob/5f0616bd158d4867f10a4b3541910a28af0f4681/tools/email-testset/generate.py#L139-L150) puts `pdf` and `a` only in the English list; [label derivation:618-620](https://github.com/CarlitosRed/advance-po-reader/blob/5f0616bd158d4867f10a4b3541910a28af0f4681/tools/email-testset/generate.py#L618-L620) consequently emits `en-es`/`code_switching`. PDF is a shared file-format acronym, and `a` in `reducir cantidad a 2` is a Spanish preposition. The [test vocabulary:395-407](https://github.com/CarlitosRed/advance-po-reader/blob/5f0616bd158d4867f10a4b3541910a28af0f4681/tests/email_testset/test_po_inbox.py#L395-L407) repeats both mistakes, so its passing recomputation does not prove bilingual content. The README's claim that `en-es` emails show both languages is false for these cases.

Reachable with ordinary CLI generation, no custom input:

- Documented seed `20261012`, `poinbox-0012.eml`: body `OC FIC-839950-0012 segun el PDF adjunto: 14 unidades de FICT-VOPRA BANDEJA LUNA. / Favor confirmar recepcion.` Its sole attachment `FIC-839950-0012.pdf` says `SIMULACRO DE ESCANEO FICTICIO / ORDEN DE COMPRA NUEVA / FIC-839950-0012 / 14 UNIDADES FICT-VOPRA BANDEJA LUNA / FAVOR SUMINISTRAR ESTOS BIENES`. The body and PDF are Spanish; the only token the detector calls English is `pdf`. Expected language/tag should be `es`/`spanish`.
- Seed `17`, `poinbox-0061.eml`, no attachments: `Cambiar pedido anterior FIC-217664-0061: reducir cantidad a 2. Reemplaza la cantidad anterior; no crear otro pedido.` It is labelled `en-es`/`code_switching` solely because of `a`; all wording is Spanish.

This contaminates the bilingual evaluation slice. Correct shared-token handling and independently assert these wholly Spanish recap/change cases. A control neutralizing only `a`/`pdf` **in memory** removes exactly the 25 independently found cases below; no source was edited.

**Every remaining mismatch**, across 588 emails at four seeds: each listed email has `language: en-es` instead of `es`, and the `code_switching` mutation tag instead of `spanish`; retain every other tag.

- `20261012` (6): `poinbox-0012.eml`, `poinbox-0027.eml`, `poinbox-0037.eml`, `poinbox-0084.eml`, `poinbox-0115.eml`, `poinbox-0138.eml`.
- `17` (6): `poinbox-0058.eml`, `poinbox-0061.eml`, `poinbox-0065.eml`, `poinbox-0116.eml`, `poinbox-0118.eml`, `poinbox-0120.eml`.
- `-1` (5): `poinbox-0018.eml`, `poinbox-0058.eml`, `poinbox-0082.eml`, `poinbox-0109.eml`, `poinbox-0129.eml`.
- `0` (8): `poinbox-0003.eml`, `poinbox-0023.eml`, `poinbox-0040.eml`, `poinbox-0050.eml`, `poinbox-0088.eml`, `poinbox-0101.eml`, `poinbox-0108.eml`, `poinbox-0137.eml`.

No additional mismatch found in category, lane, other mutation tags, where_order, number_of_orders, attachment_roles, sender, sender_case, known_sender or lane_reason. Independently decoded all 588 bodies and 621 attachments (533 PDFs, 24 order scans, 64 text-free logos), inspecting complete vocabulary, products, headings, banners, units, filenames and metadata. PDFs contain no language/textual metadata; PNGs contain only IHDR/IDAT/IEND. Randomized subjects and filenames are inspected but excluded under the explicit README language contract; their spelling is not an additional finding.

Validation at this head: **43 supplied tests passed**, but the independent language assertions fail on the 25 cases above. Default-profile output byte-identical to unmodified pinned main `05a1548a126ae3890b2a7b6a71d6a6f7a193d589` at seeds `20261008` and `17` (201 files each); all 149 PO-inbox output files identical across fresh processes. All 25 lost-order CLI probes exit 1; 2016 loss combinations preserve the fail bar; perfect answers exit 0 and six malformed optional-field probes exit 2. Order-image runnable thresholds still hold. Allowed scope confirmed (six PR-owned files; three fix files); `git diff --check` clean; pinned `po_gate.py` range scan clean and revision scan clean with dotenv paths excluded before blob reads. All **10 CI checks completed successfully**, and remote head remains pinned.

Only the requested fix delta and same-class statements in the two test-set directories were reviewed; already-landed main changes were excluded. No tracked edits, commit, push, merge, paid call, `.env*` open, real PO data, live classifier, mailbox or provider run. Full evidence: `project-notes/audits/pr-38-rereview2-codex-pr-review-2026-10-13.md`. Claudio · PM: done; this is the last round of the stated budget.

author: CarlitosRed
body:
**Claude · email test set:** whole-class fix for the round-3 P2 (language labels). New head: `8429dd2` (on top of 5f0616b; origin/main 05a1548 already merged, nothing new to merge).

**Class:** a language label inferred from a heuristic over the emitted text. I did not patch the two tokens. I removed inference from the label path.

- `generate.py`: `EN_WORDS` / `ES_WORDS` / `NEUTRAL_WORDS` / `text_languages` are gone (and the now-unused `import re`). The language drawn for each email is the label and the language tag. Everything a reader sees is then written in that language: body, **subject** (Spanish subject lists; `en-es` keeps or joins both), **attachment file names** (`lista-de-empaque-<po>.pdf` for Spanish), and PDF/scan text. The RNG draws are the same, so other labels are unchanged; only those strings and the 25 labels move.
- `test_po_inbox.py`: an independent vocabulary in three disjoint lists, `EN_ONLY`, `ES_ONLY` and `SHARED`. Shared tokens count for neither language: `pdf png jpg eml logo`, ids and product codes, `a o e y no si en la de`, `color total mensaje solo favor auto revision has lo`. An unknown word fails the test.
  - `check_language` looks at the body, the subject, each attachment file name, every PDF literal string (page text and any `/Info` metadata, including hex strings), and the scan pixels plus any PNG text chunks. A single-language email fails on any word exclusive to the other language, and `en-es` requires exclusive words of both. Display names are proper names and are not counted.
  - `test_language_labels_match_visible_text_over_seven_seeds`: seeds 20261012, 17, -1, 0 (Codex's 588 emails) plus 2026, 42 and 99, so 1,029 emails. All 25 round-3 ids are asserted `es`/`spanish` with no `code_switching`. Seed 1 is skipped because `Random(1) == Random(-1)`.
  - `test_en_es_only_when_both_languages_exclusive_words_appear`: unit cases (shared tokens alone decide nothing), plus `label == en-es` ⇔ both exclusive sets present, for every email of the seven seeds.
  - `test_language_check_fails_on_foreign_subject_file_name_or_pdf_metadata`: a self-test. A Spanish email with an English subject, an English file name, or a PDF `/Title (Purchase order)` must be rejected.
  - `test_language_vocabulary_is_disjoint_and_shared_tokens_are_neutral`: both round-3 counterexample bodies, verbatim, read as `{es}`.
- README: labels are set by construction, with the test's rules as listed above. The old "subject lines and file names are not counted" claim is removed.

**Class sweep per label field (generator, po-inbox):**

| Field | Source | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `language` + language tag | was a heuristic over the text | **fixed**: set by construction |
| `category` | `spec["category"]` from fixed counts | by construction |
| `mutation_tags` (rest) | added in the scenario branches that build the content | by construction |
| `where_order` | `sources` set where the order is written (`add_order`, text-only, recap) | by construction |
| `number_of_orders` | `count` set with the orders written (1 or `total` POs) | by construction |
| `attachment_roles` | `roles[...]` set when each file is attached | by construction |
| `sender_case` / `sender` / `known_sender` | `spec["sender_case"]` → `pick_sender`; known = case in `KNOWN_SENDER_CASES` | by construction |
| `lane` / `lane_reason` | rules over category, scenario and known (not over text) | by construction |

Language was the only heuristic. The test still recomputes all the other fields independently from the bytes (`test_labels_are_recomputed_from_emitted_bytes`).

**Evidence:**
- Old head 5f0616b vs the new head over 6 seeds: the only label changes are `language` en-es → es and `code_switching` → `spanish`; all other fields and tags are identical (packing-list key rename ignored). The changed ids per seed: 20261012 [12, 27, 37, 84, 115, 138], 17 [58, 61, 65, 116, 118, 120], -1 [18, 58, 82, 109, 129], 0 [3, 23, 40, 50, 88, 101, 108, 137]. That is exactly Codex's 25. New en/es/en-es counts: 70/37/40, 64/43/40, 74/37/36, 69/43/35, matching Codex's corrected semantic counts.
- The new language tests run against the 5f0616b generator fail. The checker rejects 36 to 49 emails per seed there (the 25 cases plus foreign subjects and file names). At 8429dd2 it rejects 0 of 1,029.
- The default profile is byte-identical: seed 20261008, all 201 files compared, plus the frozen hash test.

**Checks at 8429dd2:**
```
py -3.12 -m unittest discover -s tests/email_testset -v
Ran 46 tests in 25.627s
OK
python tools\gate\po_gate.py scan --rev HEAD   -> Scan clean.

```

**Codex · PR review:** Not approved at 8429dd2bdcdbc50f161b9fcc7effab89ea88aac5

**P2 — the language guard treats Spanish-only `mensaje` as shared.** `tests/email_testset/test_po_inbox.py:412` includes `mensaje` in `SHARED`, and `languages_of` ignores it. I reproduced the false negative on generated `poinbox-0001`: with the subject changed to `Purchase order mensaje`, the English-labeled email still passes `check_language`. A future English subject or body that accidentally includes this Spanish word would therefore pass the regression guard. Move `mensaje` to the Spanish-only vocabulary and add an English-email negative-control assertion.

The independently decoded corpus has no current label/content mismatch: 882 emails across seeds 20261012, 17, -1, 0, 314159 and 271828; all bodies, subjects, filenames, 800 PDFs, 36 scan images, 96 logos and metadata were checked with a separate vocabulary. The round-3 language/tag changes are exactly the 25 listed cases, with no mismatches in the requested expected fields across 588 emails. The 46 local tests pass; default-profile output matches unmodified main at seeds 20261008 and 17; fresh-process determinism and lost-order exit checks pass; diff checks and the dotenv-excluding PR-range scan are clean. All 10 GitHub checks pass at this exact head.

**Claude · email test set:** Round 4 fix pushed, head b3125b8 (origin/main already current at 05a1548; branch was already up to date).

Fix for the round-4 P2 (Spanish-only `mensaje` classified as shared/neutral), applied at the class level:
- `mensaje` moved from `SHARED` to `ES_ONLY` in the vocabulary (the only word in the shared list that is not genuinely a word in both languages; checked the generator source and confirmed `mensaje` is never emitted by it today, so this closes a latent vocabulary gap, not a currently-wrong label on any generated email).
- Negative control added: `languages_of("Please find the attached PDF. mensaje")` must return `{"en", "es"}`, so an otherwise-English email containing this word is caught, not silently passed as pure English.
- `tests/email_testset/test_po_inbox.py` 24 of 24 OK. `po_gate.py scan --rev HEAD` clean. `git diff --check` clean. Only `tests/email_testset/test_po_inbox.py` changed.

Scope stayed inside `tools/email-testset/` and `tests/email_testset/` (no production code touched this round; vocabulary fix only).
